name: Pakistan Sports News
tagline: Cricket first, plus the games Pakistan loves.

articles.title: Huraira and Farooq Hit Centuries as Sialkot and FATA Take Control on Day Three of Quaid-e-Azam Trophy Gold
articles.description: Mohammad Huraira's 141 and Mohammad Farooq's 123 shaped the third day of the Quaid-e-Azam Trophy Gold opening round, with Sialkot Blues declaring on 388 for five and FATA setting Lahore Whites 412 to win.
articles.sources: Cricket World, November 5, 2026; Minute Mirror, November 5, 2026
articles.body:
Mohammad Huraira and Mohammad Farooq struck centuries as Sialkot Blues and FATA strengthened their positions on the third day of the opening round of the Quaid-e-Azam Trophy Gold, which continued across Islamabad, Abbottabad and Rawalpindi on Thursday, Cricket World reported on November 5.

Sialkot declare after Huraira's 141

At the National Ground in Islamabad, Sialkot Blues resumed their second innings at 13 without loss and declared on 388 for five. Mohammad Huraira led the innings with 141, while Mohsin Riaz completed an unbeaten century as Sialkot Blues established a commanding position. Sialkot had been bowled out for 241 in their first innings, with Huraira making 117, while Karachi Blues posted 280 to take a 39-run first-innings lead — leaving Karachi chasing 349 in the final innings after Sialkot's declaration.

Farooq's 123 sets Lahore Whites 412

At the Diamond Cricket Ground in Islamabad, FATA resumed their second innings on 22 for one and were eventually dismissed for 283. Mohammad Farooq struck 123 and Salman Khan Jnr contributed 53, while Mohammad Salman Mirza claimed three wickets for Lahore Whites. Chasing 412 for victory, Lahore Whites were reduced to 40 for four by stumps. Pakistan Test captain Babar Azam remained unbeaten on 20, while Afaq Afridi took two wickets to move FATA closer to victory. In the first innings, FATA had made 362, with debutant Fawad Arshad scoring 115, before Lahore Whites were bowled out for 234, with Aamir Jamal making 74 and Babar 28.

Peshawar enforce the follow-on

At Abbottabad Cricket Stadium, Faisalabad resumed on 118 for two and were dismissed for 259 in response to Peshawar Blues' imposing first-innings total of 503 for four declared, built on Mohammad Rizwan's unbeaten 200 and Najab Khan's 133. Faisalabad were asked to follow on and reached 54 for one at stumps, with Faham-ul-Haq unbeaten on 29. At the Shoaib Akhtar Cricket Stadium in Rawalpindi, Multan resumed on 249 for seven and completed their first innings on 327. With three of the four Gold matches heading towards results on the final day, the opening round has already delivered the individual performances — Rizwan's double century, Huraira's twin hundreds across the match, and Fawad Arshad's debut century — that the domestic season is built around.

articles.title: Peshawar Whites Complete Five-Wicket Comeback as Abbottabad and AJK Also Win on Day Three of Quaid-e-Azam Trophy Silver
articles.description: Peshawar Whites staged a remarkable comeback to beat Bahawalpur by five wickets, while Abbottabad and Azad Jammu and Kashmir also secured victories on the third day of the Quaid-e-Azam Trophy Silver opening round.
articles.sources: Cricket World, November 5, 2026; Global News Pakistan, November 5, 2026
articles.body:
Peshawar Whites produced a remarkable comeback while Abbottabad and Azad Jammu and Kashmir also secured victories on the third day of the Quaid-e-Azam Trophy Silver opening round, Cricket World reported on November 5.

Peshawar Whites chase down Bahawalpur

At KCCA Stadium in Karachi, Peshawar Whites staged an impressive recovery to defeat Bahawalpur by five wickets. Bahawalpur had made 304 in their first innings, with Ali Afzal scoring 73, before Peshawar Whites replied with 219, in which Amir Azmat Barki made 88 — and Muhammad Junaid took seven wickets for 93. Peshawar Whites then reached 183 for five in 35.4 overs to complete the comeback, with Abuzar Tariq unbeaten on 75 and Mohammad Amir Azmat making 69. The win keeps Peshawar Whites firmly in contention in a competition where every pool result matters.

Abbottabad and AJK win big

In Pool B, Abbottabad secured a 105-run victory over Sialkot Whites at Dring Stadium in Bahawalpur, while at Multan Cricket Stadium, Azad Jammu and Kashmir defeated Karachi Whites by 109 runs. The results followed the day-two wins already recorded in the Silver competition: Lahore Blues beat Rawalpindi by nine wickets at the SBP Sports Complex in Karachi, chasing a 77-run target with nine wickets in hand, and Quetta beat Larkana by nine wickets at the UBL Sports Complex in Karachi after taking a 103-run first-innings lead.

The road to the final

The Quaid-e-Azam Trophy 2026-27 Silver competition features 12 regional teams competing across two pools for promotion to the Gold tier. The Silver competition continues the pathway into Pakistan's leading domestic first-class tier, with the two pool winners advancing to the five-day final in December. For the players involved — many of them young cricketers outside the national spotlight — the Silver tier is a genuine route upwards: strong performances here are watched by selectors, and the finalists will earn a place among the country's top domestic sides next season.

articles.title: Rizwan's Unbeaten Double Century Puts Peshawar in Command Against Faisalabad
articles.description: Peshawar captain Mohammad Rizwan struck an unbeaten 200 off 252 balls, with 35 fours and a six, as Peshawar declared at 503-4 on day two of their Quaid-e-Azam Trophy opener against Faisalabad.
articles.sources: Geo Super, ARY News, Wisden, Dawn, November 4, 2026
articles.body:
Peshawar captain Mohammad Rizwan struck an unbeaten double century to put his side in a commanding position against Faisalabad Region on the second day of their opening-round fixture in the Quaid-e-Azam Trophy 2026-27 at the Abbottabad Cricket Stadium on Wednesday, Geo Super and ARY News reported.

The innings

Resuming on 111 not out from 142 balls, Rizwan reached 200 off 252 deliveries, hitting 35 fours and a six, in his second first-class double hundred and his first in 12 years, Wisden reported. He shared a 246-run fourth-wicket stand with Najab Khan, who scored 133, after the pair had put on 179 on day one, and then an unbroken 130-run partnership with Muhammad Haris as Peshawar declared at 503-4 after 115.2 overs. Rizwan had come in at 127-3 on day one after being left out of Pakistan's squad for the two-match Test series against Sri Lanka starting November 9.

The state of play

In reply, Faisalabad reached 118-2 in 35.2 overs at stumps, trailing Peshawar by 385 runs. Elsewhere on day two, defending champions Karachi Blues held a slender 39-run first-innings lead over Sialkot after being bowled out for 280 in reply to 241, FATA bowled out Lahore Whites' opponents for 362 with Fawad Arshad scoring 115, and Multan took command against Islamabad on half-centuries from Imran Rafiq and Sharoon Siraj, Geo Super reported.

articles.title: Babar Azam's Controversial Dismissal Sparks DRS Row in Quaid-e-Azam Trophy
articles.description: Babar Azam was given out caught behind for 28 against FATA after replays appeared to show the ball hitting his thigh pad — and with no DRS in domestic cricket, he had no way to challenge the call.
articles.sources: Geo Super, A-Sports, ABP Live, November 4, 2026
articles.body:
Pakistan star Babar Azam was visibly disappointed after a contentious umpiring decision ended his innings for Lahore Whites against FATA in the Quaid-e-Azam Trophy on Wednesday, with the absence of the Decision Review System in domestic cricket leaving him no route to challenge it, Geo Super and A-Sports reported.

What happened

Babar, batting on 28 from 40 deliveries including six boundaries, appeared to let a delivery from FATA pacer Afaq Afridi pass his bat before wicketkeeper Rehan Afridi completed the catch behind the stumps on the final delivery of the 28th over at the Diamond Cricket Ground, Islamabad. Afaq appealed, and the on-field umpire raised his finger. Replays appeared to show the delivery making contact with Babar's thigh pad rather than his bat, reports said, and Babar pointed towards his pad to indicate the same before walking off.

The wider debate

The dismissal reignited calls for the PCB to introduce DRS in domestic competitions so players can challenge contentious calls, with fans and commentators criticising both the decision and the broadcast camera quality. Fawad Arshad led FATA's recovery with 115 off 190 deliveries as FATA were bowled out for 362, then extended their lead to 150 by stumps on day two at 22-1 in their second innings. Babar, returning to domestic first-class cricket after a disappointing ODI tri-series in which he scored 118 runs in five matches, will lead Pakistan in the Test series against Sri Lanka from November 9.

articles.title: Abdul Samad to Lead Pakistan Shaheens at Asia Cup Rising Stars 2026 in Qatar
articles.description: The PCB has named Abdul Samad captain of a 15-member Pakistan Shaheens squad for the ACC Men's Asia Cup Rising Stars 2026 in Qatar, where the defending champions open against UAE on November 20.
articles.sources: The Express Tribune, Geo Super, A-Sports, November 3, 2026
articles.body:
The Pakistan Cricket Board has announced the 15-member Pakistan Shaheens squad for the upcoming 50-over edition of the ACC Men's Asia Cup Rising Stars 2026, to be played in Qatar from November 19 to 29, The Express Tribune reported on November 3.

The squad and the group

Abdul Samad will lead defending champions Pakistan Shaheens, placed in Group B alongside India A, Nepal and the United Arab Emirates. The full squad is: Abdul Samad (captain), Ahmed Daniyal, Akif Javed, Danish Aziz, Farhan Yousuf, Haider Ali, Hasan Nawaz, Maaz Sadaqat, Mohammad Hasnain, Muhammad Imran Randhawa, Rohail Nazir (wicketkeeper), Saad Masood, Shahzaib Khan, Shamyl Hussain and Sufyan Moqim. Shaheens won the last 50-over edition in 2023 in Sri Lanka, beating India A by 128 runs.

The fixtures

Shaheens begin their campaign against UAE on November 20, face India A on November 22 and Nepal on November 24. The semi-finals are scheduled for November 26 and 27, with the final on Sunday, November 29. Reports differed slightly on whether the Nepal game is November 24 or 25, so readers should check the official fixture list for the confirmed date.

articles.title: Babar and Shaheen Headline Quaid-e-Azam Trophy Opening Round as 69th Edition Begins
articles.description: Pakistan Test captain Babar Azam and ODI skipper Shaheen Shah Afridi will headline the opening round of the 69th Quaid-e-Azam Trophy, which begins across Islamabad, Abbottabad and Rawalpindi on Tuesday.
articles.sources: Dawn, November 3, 2026
articles.body:
Pakistan Test captain Babar Azam and One-day International skipper Shaheen Shah Afridi will headline the opening round of the 69th edition of the Quaid-e-Azam Trophy, which gets under way across Islamabad, Abbottabad and Rawalpindi on Tuesday, Dawn reported on November 3.

The headline clash

Babar will turn out for Lahore Whites, who face Shaheen-led Fata at the Diamond Cricket Ground in Islamabad, in what promises to be one of the early highlights of the premier first-class competition. The Pakistan Cricket Board announced the schedule and team rosters on Monday for the Gold and Silver competitions, which will run simultaneously and feature 20 regional sides.

The format

Eight teams will compete in the Gold tier — Karachi Blues, Faisalabad, Fata, Lahore Whites, Islamabad, Peshawar Blues, Multan and Sialkot Blues — with the competition running from November 3 to December 12 and the five-day final scheduled for December 15 to 19. The 12-team Silver competition provides a pathway to the top tier for next season, with group matches from November 3 to 30 and the final between the two group winners scheduled for December 3 to 7.

articles.title: Pakistan Fined for Slow Over-Rate in Tri-Series Final Despite Title Win
articles.description: The ICC fined Pakistan 5% of its match fee after the tri-series final win over Sri Lanka, ruling the side one over short — captain Shaheen Shah Afridi pleaded guilty and accepted the sanction.
articles.sources: ICC via Dawn, Sportstar, CricTracker, November 2, 2026
articles.body:
Pakistan were fined five percent of their match fee for maintaining a slow over-rate during their three-wicket victory over Sri Lanka in the ODI tri-series final in Lahore on Saturday, the International Cricket Council said in a statement on Monday, November 2, Dawn reported.

One over short

The hosts were found to be one over short after time allowances were taken into consideration by match referee Jeff Crowe of the Emirates ICC Elite Panel. Under Article 2.22 of the ICC Code of Conduct, players are fined five percent of their match fee for every over their side fails to bowl in the allotted time. On-field umpires Ahsan Raza and Wayne Knights, third umpire Sharfuddoula Ibne Shahid and fourth umpire Rashid Riaz levelled the charges. Captain Shaheen Shah Afridi pleaded guilty and accepted the proposed sanction, so there was no need for a formal hearing.

A second offence in the same tournament

The Lahore final was not Pakistan's first slow over-rate offence in the tri-series: in the tournament opener at Rawalpindi on October 18, also against Sri Lanka, Pakistan fell two overs short and were docked 10 percent of their match fee. The penalty does not change the result — Pakistan chased 326 with nine balls to spare, Fakhar Zaman scoring 127 off 99 balls — but it closes the disciplinary file on a tournament Pakistan otherwise dominated, losing only one match, against England.

articles.title: After the Tri-Series Triumph, Pakistan Turn to Tests Against Sri Lanka on November 9
articles.description: Pakistan will now play a two-match Test series against Sri Lanka starting on November 9, carrying momentum from a first home tri-series title since 2008 — and a new-look batting core that played without fear.
articles.sources: ETV Bharat, The Express Tribune, November 2, 2026
articles.body:
Pakistan will now play a two-match Test series against Sri Lanka starting on November 9, following their ODI tri-series triumph in Lahore, ETV Bharat reported on November 2.

What the tri-series showed

The Express Tribune's editorial on November 2 called the tri-series win — also featuring England — a major turning point, and Pakistan's first tri-series title since 2008. New batters Hassan Nawaz, Saad Baig and Maaz Sadaqat played without fear, all-rounder Arafat Minhas brought energy, and the fast-bowling trio of Shaheen Shah Afridi, Haris Rauf and Naseem Shah worked together to dismantle batting lineups. The final belonged to veteran Fakhar Zaman, whose 127 off 99 balls, with 11 fours and six sixes, made a chase of 326 look comfortable.

What the Tests will test

The red-ball series will ask different questions of the same core: patience, discipline and depth over five days rather than one-day explosiveness. Sri Lanka, beaten in the Lahore final after posting 325 for 8, will look to Kamindu Mendis — who led their final batting effort — to anchor their reply. Full squads, venues and session timings for the Tests had not been detailed in the reports checked at writing time; readers should check the official series announcement for confirmed fixtures.

articles.title: Fakhar Zaman's 127 Powers Pakistan to Tri-Series Title in Record-Equalling 326 Chase
articles.description: Fakhar Zaman's 127 off 99 balls led Pakistan to a three-wicket win over Sri Lanka in the ODI tri-series final at Gaddafi Stadium, Lahore, chasing down 326 with nine balls to spare.
articles.sources: Express Tribune, Oman Observer, NDTV, November 1, 2026
articles.body:
Pakistan beat Sri Lanka by three wickets in the final of the ODI tri-series at Gaddafi Stadium, Lahore, on Saturday, October 31, chasing down a challenging 326-run target with nine balls to spare to lift the title, The Express Tribune and Oman Observer reported on November 1.

Fakhar leads the recovery

Sri Lanka, sent in to bat after Pakistan won the toss, posted 325 for 8, built on Kamindu Mendis's maiden ODI century of 131 off 128 balls and Pavan Rathnayake's 77, the pair sharing a 146-run third-wicket partnership. Pakistan's chase began disastrously, with Maaz Sadaqat out for 5 and Babar Azam for 0 with the total at 14. Fakhar Zaman then struck a commanding 127 off 99 balls, with 11 fours and six sixes, his 12th ODI century, completing 4,000 ODI runs when he reached 108, and sharing a 149-run third-wicket partnership with Saad Baig, who scored 74 off 75 balls for his maiden ODI half-century.

A finish sealed with a six

With Pakistan five wickets down for 230, Arafat Minhas smashed a quickfire 61 off 31 balls, with four sixes and three fours, and put on 94 for the sixth wicket with Hasan Nawaz, who remained unbeaten on 37 off 45 balls. Minhas fell with Pakistan on 324 and Faheem Ashraf was dismissed for a first-ball duck, before captain Shaheen Shah Afridi, unbeaten on 6, hit the winning six to take Pakistan to 331 for 7 in 48.3 overs. The chase equalled the record for the highest successful run chase in an ODI final, matching India's 326 against England at Lord's in 2002, and gave Pakistan its first tri-series title at home after failing in the finals of 1994, 2004 and 2025, according to the Oman Observer.

articles.title: Abbas Afridi's 73 Off 16 Balls Seals Hong Kong Sixes Plate Title for Pakistan
articles.description: Captain Abbas Afridi smashed an unbeaten 73 off 16 balls as Pakistan beat Oman by 18 runs in the Plate final of the Hong Kong Sixes on Sunday, finishing fifth overall.
articles.sources: Express Tribune, Geo Super, Daily Pakistan, November 1, 2026
articles.body:
Pakistan defeated Oman by 18 runs in the Plate final of the Hong Kong Sixes 2026 at Mission Road Ground, Mong Kok, on Sunday, November 1, to claim the second-tier title, The Express Tribune, Geo Super and Daily Pakistan reported.

Afridi's blitz sets up 154

Batting first after Oman elected to field, Pakistan piled up 154 for 4 in their allotted six overs. Captain Abbas Afridi led the charge with a blistering unbeaten 73 off just 16 deliveries, hitting one four and 11 sixes, retiring before returning to the crease in the final over. Ahmed Daniyal smashed 25 off five balls, including four sixes, Muhammad Shahzad made 13 off four balls with two sixes, and opener Khawaja Nafay scored seven off three balls, including a six.

Oman fall 18 runs short

In reply, Oman managed 136 for 4 in their six overs despite a strong opening partnership between Usman Ali and Zohaib Amanat. Usman top-scored with 67 off 17 balls, hitting four fours and eight sixes, while Amanat made 61 off 18 balls. Afridi was named player of the match. The Plate victory gave the six-time champions a fifth-place finish overall after they failed to defend their main title, having finished second behind the UAE in Group C; Afghanistan won the main Cup title for the first time, beating Australia by four wickets in the final.

articles.title: Sri Lanka Set Pakistan 326 to Win the ODI Tri-Series Final in Lahore
articles.description: Sri Lanka posted 325 for 8 in the tri-series final at Gaddafi Stadium on Saturday, with Kamindu Mendis scoring a magnificent 131, leaving Pakistan chasing 326 for the trophy.
articles.sources: Geo News, Aaj TV, Outlook India live coverage, October 31, 2026
articles.body:
Sri Lanka set Pakistan a 326-run target in the final of the ODI tri-series at Lahore's Gaddafi Stadium on Saturday, October 31, after Pakistan won the toss and elected to field first, Geo News and Aaj TV reported.

Kamindu's maiden ODI century

Openers Avishka Fernando and Kamindu Mendis put on a 50-run partnership before Fernando departed for 38 off 49 deliveries, ending an 87-run opening stand. Kamindu continued to lead the charge and reached his maiden ODI century, eventually departing for 131 off 128 deliveries, featuring 12 fours and two sixes, after captain Shaheen Shah Afridi trapped him lbw, ending a 146-run third-wicket partnership with Pavan Rathnayake.

A chase under way in Lahore

Asitha Fernando and Maheesh Theekshana added valuable runs in the final two overs to take Sri Lanka to 325 for 8. For Pakistan, Naseem Shah and Haris Rauf picked up two wickets each. At the time of writing, Pakistan's chase was under way, with Fakhar Zaman bringing up his 12th ODI century — joining Saeed Anwar as only the second Pakistani batter to score two hundreds in an ODI final — and Pakistan at 193 for 3 after 30 overs, according to live coverage. The final result was not yet decided when this article was published; readers should check the live scoreboard for the outcome.

articles.title: Pakistan Beat Hong Kong to Reach Hong Kong Sixes Plate Final Against Oman
articles.description: Pakistan defeated hosts Hong Kong by five wickets in the Plate semi-final of the Hong Kong Sixes on Saturday, setting up a final against Oman on Sunday.
articles.sources: Geo Super, October 31, 2026
articles.body:
Pakistan defeated the host country by five wickets in the second Plate semi-final of the Hong Kong Sixes 2026 at Mission Road Ground, Mong Kok, on Saturday, to set up a final against Oman, Geo Super reported.

Abbas Afridi's blitz

Batting first, Hong Kong posted 106 for 3 in their allotted six overs. In reply, Pakistan chased down the 107-run target in just 4.3 overs, losing five wickets in the process. Captain Abbas Afridi once again led from the front with a sensational 55 off just 13 deliveries, smashing three fours and seven sixes. Following Afridi's retirement, Abdul Samad contributed a quickfire 17 off four deliveries, striking one four and two sixes to complete the chase.

From group disappointment to a Plate final

Six-time champions and defending title-holders Pakistan had earlier been eliminated from contention for the main Cup trophy after finishing second in Group C, as only group winners qualify for the main Cup semi-finals. Pakistan suffered a last-ball defeat against the UAE in their opening fixture on Friday, then bounced back emphatically against India, restricting their arch-rivals to 88 for 5 before completing the chase in just 3.5 overs. They will now face Oman in Sunday's Plate final.

articles.title: Pakistan Thrash India by Four Wickets at Hong Kong Sixes, Chasing 89 in 3.5 Overs
articles.description: Defending champions Pakistan bounced back from an earlier defeat to beat India by four wickets at the Hong Kong Sixes 2026, chasing down 89 in just 3.5 overs at Mong Kok on October 30.
articles.sources: The Indian Express, CricTracker and ProPakistani, October 30, 2026.
articles.body:
Pakistan, the defending champions, registered their first victory of the Hong Kong Sixes 2026 by defeating arch-rivals India by four wickets at the Mission Road Ground in Mong Kok on October 30. Pakistan chased a target of 89 in just 3.5 overs to register the win.

India's innings stalls at 88

Pakistan captain Abbas Afridi won the toss and elected to bowl first. India were restricted to 88 for five in their six overs, the lowest score posted by any side on the opening day of the tournament. Shashank Singh was the lone bright spot with the bat, hammering 40 runs off 11 balls, including two fours and five sixes, after a top-order collapse.

Afridi's five sixes in the opening over

Chasing 89, Pakistan made an explosive start as captain Abbas Afridi smashed five consecutive sixes in the opening over bowled by his counterpart Krunal Pandya, helping his team collect 31 runs. Afridi combined with Khawaja Nafay to plunder 28 runs off T. Natarajan's bowling, reaching 73 for one at the halfway stage. Nafay struck 41 off 12 balls, while Afridi made 35 off just eight deliveries, before Irfan Khan took Pakistan home with 13 balls remaining. Pakistan finished on 92 for two, and Afridi was named Player of the Match.

What it means for Group C

The win was especially significant because Pakistan had lost their opening Group C match to the United Arab Emirates by one wicket earlier in the day, leaving them on the brink of elimination. The Hong Kong Sixes 2026 features 12 teams divided into four groups of three, with the group winners advancing to the Cup semi-finals and the final set for November 1. India, now at the bottom of Group C, must beat the UAE on October 31 by a big margin to stay alive.

For the defending champions, the victory keeps their title defence on track — and delivers one of the most one-sided chases in the tournament's recent history.

articles.title: Aamer Jamal's 7-32 and Fifty Lead Markhor to President's Trophy Final Win
articles.description: All-rounder Aamer Jamal took 7 for 32 and scored 55 from number eight as Markhor IT Solutions beat State Bank of Pakistan to lift the President's Trophy on October 30, 2026.
articles.sources: Wisden, October 30, 2026.
articles.body:
Aamer Jamal delivered an all-round performance in the President's Trophy final to help Markhor IT Solutions lift the trophy on Friday, October 30, according to Wisden. Having been bowled out for just 112 batting first, Markhor needed an inspiring performance to get back into the game — and Jamal provided it.

Seven wickets to turn the final

Jamal snared 7 for 32 in the first innings to bowl out State Bank of Pakistan for 172, keeping the deficit to just 60. The seam-bowling all-rounder delivered 14 overs in the innings, including four maidens, in a spell that dragged his side back into the contest.

A fifty from number eight

He then starred with the bat as well, scoring 55 from number eight after Atizaz Habib Khan was retired hurt. He was the second top run-getter in the innings behind Abuzar Tariq's 85, powering the side to 296 and setting a defendable target of 237. The bowling unit did the rest to bundle out SBP for 185, with Khalid Usman taking four for 38, while Jamal took a solitary wicket in the second innings after bowling 14 overs for 39 runs.

A response to his Test axing

The 30-year-old all-rounder played only three games in the tournament, scoring 118 runs and picking up 10 wickets at an average of 18.20. Jamal was notably one of the seven players sent home from England in the middle of the tour after Pakistan lost the second Test at Lord's by 194 runs, and he could not find a spot in Pakistan's squad for the upcoming two-Test series against Sri Lanka. He has played nine Tests to date, managing 355 runs at an average of 23.66 with two fifties and 23 wickets at 35.21 apiece with two five-wicket hauls.

A match-winning final like this one is exactly the kind of statement a player on the outer makes — and selectors will have noticed.

articles.title: England Meet Sri Lanka in Lahore as Tri-Series Builds to October 31 Final
articles.description: England face Sri Lanka in Lahore on October 29 in the last league match of the tri-series, with the final set for Gaddafi Stadium on October 31, 2026.
articles.sources: Public news reports, October 2026.
articles.body:
England meet Sri Lanka in Lahore on Thursday in the final league match of the ODI tri-series, the last fixture before the tournament final at Gaddafi Stadium on Saturday, October 31. The seven-match tournament, featuring Pakistan, England and Sri Lanka, has been played in Rawalpindi and Lahore from October 18 to 31.

How the series has unfolded

Sri Lanka booked their place in the final with a commanding eight-wicket victory over Pakistan in Lahore on October 27. After winning the toss and opting to bowl, Sri Lanka's pacers dismantled Pakistan's batting line-up, with left-arm quick Dilshan Madushanka delivering a spell of 5 for 34. Pakistan were bowled out for 110 in 25.3 overs, with Babar Azam top-scoring with 29, before Sri Lanka chased the target down in 18.1 overs, finishing at 114 for 2, led by Kamindu Mendis with an unbeaten 62.

What Thursday's match means

Thursday's Lahore fixture is the last chance for the sides to settle the final line-up before Saturday's decider. The series is captained by Shaheen Shah Afridi for Pakistan, Harry Brook for England and Kusal Mendis for Sri Lanka, and it serves as preparation for the 2027 ODI World Cup, which South Africa, Zimbabwe and Namibia will host.

The road to the final

The tournament comprised six league matches followed by the final, with the opening fixtures in Rawalpindi before the action moved to Lahore. The final at Gaddafi Stadium on October 31 will bring the curtain down on a home season that continues with two Tests against Sri Lanka in November.

Supporters should check official listings for the exact start time of Thursday's day-night fixture.

articles.title: Pakistan Beat Hong Kong in Padel Qualifier but Miss Out on World Cup
articles.description: Pakistan ended their FIP World Cup qualifying campaign with a 2-1 win over Hong Kong in Kuwait City, but earlier losses to Saudi Arabia and Kuwait ended their hopes.
articles.sources: Public news reports, October 2026.
articles.body:
Pakistan defeated Hong Kong 2-1 in their final Group C tie in Kuwait City, but failed to qualify for the FIP World Cup 2026 after losing their opening two ties against Saudi Arabia and Kuwait in the Asia-Africa qualifiers, according to reports published on October 29, 2026.

A winning finish

Pakistan secured victories in the first two matches against Hong Kong at Oro Padel to clinch the tie, finishing their campaign with a win after a difficult start. Huzaifa Abdul Rehman and Huzaima Abdul Rehman gave Pakistan a strong start, defeating Hong Kong's J. McKee and T. Y. A. Yao 6-1, 6-1 in the opening match. Abdullah Adnan and Muhammad Salar extended Pakistan's lead by winning the second match. Hong Kong avoided a clean sweep as A. Khan and S. Z. Lo Escoto defeated Danish Ahmed and Muhammad Azhar 6-1, 6-1 in the third match.

Where qualification slipped away

Pakistan had earlier lost 1-2 to Saudi Arabia in their opening tie on October 26, despite a victory by Huzaifa Abdul Rehman and Huzaima, and then suffered a 0-3 defeat against Kuwait on October 27, with Kuwait winning all three matches. Those two results left Pakistan unable to advance, even with the closing win over Hong Kong.

How the qualifiers work

The Asia-Africa qualifiers, held from October 26 to 30, feature 14 men's national teams divided into four groups. The group winners advance to the knockout stage to determine the qualifying teams for the FIP World Cup 2026, scheduled to take place in Doha, Qatar, from November 2 to 7.

For Pakistan's padel squad, the campaign ends with a consolation victory and a clear lesson: in a short group format, the opening ties decide everything.

articles.title: Sri Lanka Crush Pakistan by Eight Wickets to Reach Tri-Series Final
articles.description: Dilshan Madushanka's 5 for 34 bowled Pakistan out for 110 as Sri Lanka won by eight wickets in Lahore to book a place in the October 31 tri-series final.
articles.sources: News Today, Outlook India, October 28, 2026
articles.body:
Sri Lanka stormed into the final of the ODI tri-series with a commanding eight-wicket victory over Pakistan at the Gaddafi Stadium in Lahore on Tuesday, knocking England out of contention. Left-arm pacer Dilshan Madushanka led the bowling attack with career-best figures of five for 34 as Pakistan were bundled out for just 110 in 25.3 overs after electing to bat.

A one-sided afternoon

Babar Azam top-scored for Pakistan with 29, but the hosts struggled to build partnerships and lost wickets at regular intervals; Sahan Arachchige provided valuable support with two wickets for 24 runs. Sri Lanka chased down the modest target in just 18.1 overs, finishing at 114 for two, with Kamindu Mendis anchoring the innings with an unbeaten 62 off 60 balls and Pavan Rathnayake remaining not out on 23.

The victory secured Sri Lanka's place in the October 31 final against Pakistan, who had already qualified after winning their first three matches, and ended England's hopes of reaching the title clash. Sri Lanka will face England in their final league match on Thursday before meeting Pakistan again in the final, where the hosts will need a very different batting performance.

articles.title: Haris Rauf Fined 20% of Match Fee, Nears Suspension After ICC Code Breach
articles.description: The ICC fined Pakistan pacer Haris Rauf 20% of his match fee and added a demerit point, taking his tally to five, after an on-field confrontation with England's Will Jacks.
articles.sources: The Business Standard, ABP Live, October 28, 2026
articles.body:
Pakistan fast bowler Haris Rauf has been fined 20% of his match fee and issued an official reprimand for breaching the ICC code of conduct during his team's one-wicket victory over England in the ODI tri-series, the International Cricket Council said on Wednesday. Rauf also received one demerit point, his third offence within 24 months, taking his total to five points and moving him closer to a suspension.

What happened in the 46th over

The incident occurred during the 46th over of Pakistan's run chase when Rauf, standing at the non-striker's end, appealed for a wide and then exchanged words with England all-rounder Will Jacks. According to the ICC, Rauf breached Article 2.2, covering conduct contrary to the spirit of the game: he raised his bat and continued the argument despite warnings from umpire Sharfuddoula Ibne Shahid, and brushed past the umpire while walking towards Jacks.

England were also sanctioned, fined 15% of their match fee for maintaining a bowling rate three overs below the required target; captain Harry Brook accepted the offence, so no formal hearing was required. The match itself produced a dramatic finish: England posted 242, Pakistan slumped to 154 for 9, and Shadab Khan's unbeaten 113, shared in an 89-run last-wicket partnership with Rauf, stunned the visitors. The disciplinary action is now an unwelcome subplot ahead of Saturday's final.

articles.title: Pakistan Begin Hong Kong Sixes Title Defence Under Abbas Afridi
articles.description: Defending champions Pakistan head to the Hong Kong Sixes 2026, starting October 30, with Mohammad Abbas Afridi named captain of a seven-player squad placed in Group C alongside India and the UAE.
articles.sources: Geo News, October 2026; IPL.com, October 2026.
articles.body:
Pakistan will compete in the Hong Kong Sixes 2026 from October 30 to November 1 at the Tin Kwong Road Recreation Ground in Hong Kong, entering the tournament as defending champions after winning the 2025 edition. The Pakistan Cricket Board announced a seven-player squad on October 9, with Mohammad Abbas Afridi named captain.

Twelve teams will contest the fast-paced six-a-side format, divided into four groups of three. Pakistan have been placed in Group C alongside India and the United Arab Emirates, and will begin their campaign against the UAE on October 30 before facing India later the same day. The team is scheduled to depart for Hong Kong on October 28.

The squad

Alongside captain Abbas Afridi, the squad features batter Abdul Samad, all-rounders Ahmed Daniyal and Saad Masood, batter Muhammad Irfan Khan, wicketkeeper Khawaja Nafay and batter Muhammad Shahzad, with Raza Kitchlew as team manager. The compact squad reflects the six-a-side format, where every player must contribute with bat, ball and in the field.

Pakistan clinched the title last year, their sixth overall, by defeating Kuwait in the final, and will aim to retain the trophy against a strong international field. Australia, hosts Hong Kong China and England make up Group A, while Bangladesh, Scotland and Sri Lanka are in Group B, and South Africa, Oman and Afghanistan form Group D.

Format and knockout path

The opening day will feature nine matches, with group-stage fixtures completed on October 31. The top-ranked team from each group will progress to the Cup semi-finals, the second-placed sides will contest the Plate semi-finals, and the third-placed teams will compete in the Bowl semi-finals. For Pakistan, the group clash with India on the opening day is the standout fixture, and a strong start against the UAE will be key to topping the group and keeping the title defence on track.

articles.title: Malaysia Edge Pakistan on Penalties to Win Sultan of Johor Cup
articles.description: Malaysia came from two goals down to beat Pakistan 4-3 in a penalty shootout and win the Sultan of Johor Cup 2026 after an entertaining final ended 2-2 in Johor Bahru.
articles.sources: The Express Tribune, October 24, 2026; Dawn, October 23, 2026.
articles.body:
Malaysia staged a remarkable comeback to defeat Pakistan in a penalty shootout and win the Sultan of Johor Cup 2026 after an entertaining final ended 2-2 at the Taman Daya Hockey Stadium. The hosts held their nerve to triumph 4-3 in the shootout, denying Pakistan the title after recovering from a two-goal deficit in regulation time.

Pakistan appeared firmly in control after penalty-corner specialist Rana Waleed opened the scoring in the 19th minute. Usman Muhammad extended their advantage four minutes later, scoring a field goal to put Pakistan 2-0 ahead and leave Malaysia facing an uphill battle.

Malaysia fight back

The hosts responded quickly to reignite their hopes. Adam Asyraf Johari converted a penalty corner in the 25th minute, reducing the deficit to 2-1 and giving Malaysia renewed momentum. Malaysia continued to push forward after the break against a determined Pakistan defence, and their persistence paid off in the 49th minute when Dheeressh Gunaseelan scored from a penalty corner to bring the hosts level at 2-2.

Neither side could find a decisive goal during the remaining regulation time, forcing the final into a penalty shootout. Malaysia proved more clinical from the spot, converting four attempts through Johari, Gagandeep Singh, Rahuul Fazrien Muhammad Nazrien and Ashrafeel Iman Mohd Rizal. Pakistan scored three times, with Ali Hamza converting once and Waleed finding the net twice.

Road to the final

Pakistan's junior team had qualified for the final after holding Japan to a 2-2 draw in their final round-robin match at the same venue. Hamza Fayyaz and Ghulam Mustafa scored for Pakistan, who twice came from behind to secure the draw and book their place in the title clash. Both teams finished the league stage with seven points and an identical goal difference of plus eight, but Pakistan advanced on a superior goals-scored record, having netted 18 goals against Japan's 16.

Pakistan concluded the preliminary round with two wins, one draw and one defeat, having earlier beaten China 8-3 and Canada 6-2 before suffering a narrow 3-2 loss to hosts Malaysia. The final defeat marked Pakistan's second runners-up finish in the Sultan of Johor Cup, having also finished second in the 2016 edition.

articles.title: Saim Ayub Released from ODI Squad as Sahibzada Farhan Named Replacement
articles.description: The PCB confirmed on October 26 that opener Saim Ayub has been released from Pakistan's ODI squad for the remainder of the tri-series, with Sahibzada Farhan named as his replacement.
articles.sources: Cricbuzz, October 26, 2026; The Tribune (India), October 26, 2026; India TV News, October 26, 2026.
articles.body:
The Pakistan Cricket Board confirmed on October 26 that opening batter Saim Ayub has been released from Pakistan's men's ODI squad for the remainder of the ongoing tri-series, after he requested a return to domestic cricket to work on his batting form and regain confidence. The national selection committee has named Sahibzada Farhan as Ayub's replacement for the remainder of the series.

An honest conversation

According to the PCB statement, Ayub expressed his desire to return to domestic cricket following a conversation with head coach Mike Hesson. The board said it respected Ayub's decision and appreciated his honest assessment of his current form, and that the team management and the selection committee mutually agreed to accept his request. Ayub, 24, managed scores of 6, 8 and 7 in his three innings in the tournament, according to Cricbuzz, a run of low scores that left his place under scrutiny even before Monday's announcement.

Farhan steps in

Farhan, the newly appointed T20I captain, was originally not picked for the ODI tri-series squad. His inclusion comes as Pakistan seek greater output from their leading batters: reports noted that Ayub, Fakhar Zaman and Babar Azam have collectively averaged just 15.11 in the tri-series, while Pakistan's overall top-order average of 19.81 is the lowest among ODI teams this year. Farhan's arrival therefore carries a clear brief, to steady the top of the order at a moment when the middle order has repeatedly been left to rescue innings, most recently in the dramatic one-wicket win over England on Sunday that secured Pakistan's place in the final.

The road to the final

Pakistan have already qualified for the final after winning their first three matches. They will face Sri Lanka in the fifth match of the tri-series at Gaddafi Stadium in Lahore on Tuesday, October 27, before the final on October 31. Captain Shaheen Afridi had hinted at possible adjustments following the England victory, and Monday's change is the first of them. Pakistan had also added top-order batter Maaz Sadaqat to the squad on Sunday, replacing left-arm wristspinner Sufyan Moqim shortly before the England match.

What it means for Ayub

For Ayub, the release is framed by the PCB as a reset rather than a rejection, a chance to score runs in domestic cricket away from the pressure of an international series. Reports noted, however, that he has no immediate scheduled domestic fixture apart from the President's Trophy final beginning October 27, in which he is not involved, with his next opportunity possibly coming in November at the Quaid-e-Azam Trophy. That gap makes the timing of his return to form an open question, and his international future will depend on the runs he scores when that domestic window opens.

articles.title: Egyptians Sweep Both Titles at Karachi Venus Squash Open
articles.description: Egypt's Karim El Hammamy and Rowan Elaraby won the men's and women's titles respectively at the Venus ABC Open squash championship in Karachi on Sunday.
articles.sources: Pakistan Archive, October 26, 2026; Sindh Squash Association.
articles.body:
Egypt's Karim El Hammamy and Rowan Elaraby won the men's and women's titles respectively at the Venus ABC Open International Squash Championship in Karachi on Sunday, completing an Egyptian sweep of both trophies at the copper-level event. The finals were played at the Asif Nawaz Squash Complex of the Defence Authority Creek Club in Karachi, with squash legend Jahangir Khan reported to be present for the closing day.

El Hammamy takes the men's title

El Hammamy, the second seed, beat top seed Curtis Malik of England 11-6, 12-10, 11-3 in 48 minutes in the men's final. The scoreline tells the story of a match that was competitive in the second game, which El Hammamy edged 12-10, but otherwise controlled by the Egyptian. Malik, as top seed, had been expected to push hard for the title, but El Hammamy's consistency and movement around the court gave him the edge in the rallies that mattered, and the third game ran away from the Englishman at 11-3.

Elaraby completes the sweep

In the women's final, fourth seed Elaraby beat compatriot and second seed Amina El Rihany 11-6, 11-8, 11-5 in 33 minutes, completing the Egyptian sweep. The all-Egyptian final underlined the depth of Egyptian squash, which has dominated the world game for years across both the men's and women's tours. Elaraby's win, achieved in straight games, was the quicker of the two finals, but it still required her to hold her nerve against a higher-seeded compatriot who knew her game well.

Prize money and prestige

Both winners received 5,415 dollars each in prize money along with the trophy, according to the Sindh Squash Association. Copper-level events on the international circuit may not carry the prize money of the sport's biggest tournaments, but they are vital stepping stones: ranking points earned here help players climb towards larger events, and for Karachi, hosting an international field is itself a statement about the city's squash infrastructure and its history in the sport.

Why Karachi matters for squash

Karachi's place in squash history is inseparable from Jahangir Khan, whose presence at the finals linked the present to the era when Pakistan ruled world squash. Events like the Venus Open keep that tradition alive, giving local fans a chance to watch international squash at home and giving young Pakistani players a benchmark for the standard required at the top level. Egypt's sweep may have disappointed local hopes for a home winner, but the quality of the finals, and the smooth staging of the event, will encourage organisers to bring more international squash back to the city.

articles.title: Shadab Khan's Unbeaten 113 Lifts Pakistan Past England in One-Wicket Tri-Series Thriller
articles.description: Chasing 242 from 154-9, Shadab and Haris Rauf shared a record 89-run last-wicket stand to book Pakistan's place in the tri-series final at Lahore.
articles.sources: Reuters, October 25, 2026; The Express Tribune; ESPNcricinfo.
articles.body:
Pakistan all-rounder Shadab Khan struck an unbeaten 113 and shared a record 89-run last-wicket stand with Haris Rauf as the hosts rallied from 154-9 to secure a one-wicket win over England in Lahore on Sunday and book their place in the tri-series final. Chasing 242 for victory, Pakistan appeared to be heading towards defeat after England's bowlers reduced them to 154-9 in the 34th over — and then produced one of the great ODI escapes.

England's innings: Duckett stands alone

Earlier, England were bowled out for 241 in 46.4 overs despite Ben Duckett's composed 105. Shaheen Shah Afridi led Pakistan's bowling effort with 4-46 to dismantle England's top order, striking in the opening over to dismiss Tom Banton before removing Joe Root in the third over, while Jordan Cox fell to Haris Rauf as England slumped to 52-4. Ben Duckett and Sam Curran steadied the innings with a fifth-wicket partnership of 93; Curran made 42 before becoming Afridi's third victim. Jamie Overton helped take England past 200, while Gus Atkinson finished unbeaten on 36. The defeat was England's third successive loss in the tri-series after Sri Lanka completed the second-highest successful run chase in ODI history, reaching a target of 430 with one ball to spare.

Pakistan's collapse — and then the impossible

Pakistan lost Fakhar Zaman and Babar Azam for 10 apiece before Saad Baig struck a brisk 32 off 22 balls and Salman Ali Agha made 26 to briefly revive the chase. Shadab Khan came to the crease in the 24th over with the hosts struggling at 103-6, and by the 34th over Pakistan were 154-9, with a full-house Gaddafi Stadium largely emptied. What followed was extraordinary. Shadab launched a superb counter-attack and, with Rauf making an unbeaten seven off 19 balls, guided the hosts to victory with 17 balls to spare. Their 89-run partnership was the highest for the final wicket in a successful ODI run chase, and Shadab's score was also the highest individual score in ODI history by a batter batting at number eight or lower. Shadab struck 13 fours and five sixes in his 96-ball innings.

The review that saved the match

The drama peaked when Shadab was given out lbw to Atkinson with 21 runs needed, but successfully reviewed the decision after replays showed an inside edge. Restored to the crease, he took Pakistan to the finish line, with Rauf hitting debutant quick Henry Crocombe for the winning boundary. Seamers Gus Atkinson (2-62), Jamie Overton (3-43) and spinner Liam Dawson (2-30) had all but wrapped up the game — until the last-wicket pair rewrote it. Pakistan are into the final; England, who must now win against Sri Lanka to have any chance of joining them, are left to wonder how a match they had won slipped away.

articles.title: Babar Azam to Lead New-Look Pakistan Test Squad Against Sri Lanka
articles.description: Mohammad Rizwan, Imam-ul-Haq and Shan Masood are dropped as three uncapped players earn call-ups for the two-Test home series in Rawalpindi and Lahore.
articles.sources: Outlook India, October 24, 2026; The Express Tribune; Dawn.
articles.body:
Pakistan on 24 October 2026 named a 14-member squad for their two-Test home series against Sri Lanka, with Babar Azam appointed captain in Rawalpindi and Lahore. The selection is a sharp break with the recent past: Shan Masood, Mohammad Rizwan and Imam-ul-Haq were left out of the squad, Salman Ali Agha is back, and three uncapped players have earned maiden Test call-ups.

The omissions that dominate the debate

Former captain Masood, Rizwan and Imam have all been left out of the squad. Rizwan and Imam are still under investigation over their conduct on the England tour, which makes their absence from this series more notable. Masood's exclusion also draws attention: he was said to be 'fearful' of a possible drop, despite his 90 in the series finale against England. Ten players from Pakistan's England tour have been omitted from the initial squad in total, including Aamir Jamal, Khurram Shahzad, Mohammad Ali, Sajid Khan, Abdullah Shafique and Ubaid Shah. The PCB announcement did not specify individual reasons for the exclusions, beyond the reported investigations concerning Rizwan and Imam.

The new faces, and a returning one

Left-handed batsman Mohammad Taha and Mohammad Suleman, along with promising batsman Sameer Minhas, have received their maiden call-ups following impressive performances in domestic cricket. Taha, 26, is the leading run-scorer in the ongoing President's Trophy Grade-I first-class tournament, having amassed 730 runs in seven matches, including three centuries with 225 being his highest score. Suleman has scored 652 runs in the same competition, also hitting three centuries, while Sameer has made 405 runs in seven matches during his maiden first-class season after impressing with Pakistan's Under-19 side. Salman Ali Agha is back in the squad after Pakistan left him out during the August-September tour of England; he answered with a triple century and a century for Kingsmen Academy in the ongoing President's Trophy Grade-I 2026/27.

What the series looks like

The ICC World Test Championship series will be played in Rawalpindi and Lahore from November 9 to 21, with the first Test at Rawalpindi Cricket Stadium from November 9 to 13 and the second at Gaddafi Stadium in Lahore from November 17 to 21. Babar will be joined by Abdullah Fazal, Arafat Minhas, Azan Awais, Mohammad Abbas, wicketkeepers Mohammad Ghazi Ghori and Saad Baig, Razaullah and Saud Shakeel, who have retained their places, with Ali Usman also included. Two more fast bowlers will be added to the squad from the PCB Patron's XI after a three-day warm-up match against Sri Lanka from November 4 to 6 at the Islamabad Club. Earlier on Saturday, PCB chairman Mohsin Naqvi described the Test squad as full of young blood — and against Sri Lanka, that youth gets its examination.

articles.title: Pakistan's Pink Day: Green Shirts Wear Pink Against England for Breast Cancer Awareness
articles.description: At Gaddafi Stadium, Lahore, Pakistan swapped green for pink on October 25, with pink stumps, pink ribbons and free screenings for fans from October 24 to 26.
articles.sources: Wisden; The Express Tribune; ABP Live, October 25, 2026.
articles.body:
Pakistan players donned pink jerseys in the ODI tri-series fixture against England at Gaddafi Stadium, Lahore, on Sunday, October 25, as the Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) dedicated the match to breast cancer awareness. Pakistan's familiar green kit made way for a striking shade of pink, but there was a meaningful reason behind the team's change of colours — and the gesture extended far beyond the shirts.

A stadium turns pink

The Pakistan Cricket Board has organised Breast Cancer Awareness Day as part of its corporate social responsibility initiatives, during October, which is internationally observed as Breast Cancer Awareness Month. This Pink Day fixture between Pakistan and England serves as a medium to highlight the importance of early detection and adequate treatment. The PCB partnered with Pink Ribbon Pakistan, and the campaign was not limited to the team's playing kit: the stumps used for the game were also pink, the big screens and LED boards displayed awareness messages throughout the day, and players from both sides, match officials and coaching staff wore pink ribbons during the game. Educational segments and survivor stories were also featured on the stadium's big screens and during the broadcast.

Why cricket is the platform

"The Pakistan Cricket Board recognises the responsibility that comes with the immense following and influence of cricket in our country," said the PCB COO Sumair Ahmad Syed. "Through this Pink Ribbon initiative, we want to use the platform of international cricket to raise awareness about breast cancer and highlight the importance of early detection and timely medical attention." The logic is straightforward: a high-profile international fixture reaches an audience that health messaging alone rarely does, and it reaches families watching together. By dedicating an international fixture to the cause, the board hopes to reach a wider audience and highlight the importance of seeking medical guidance and undergoing appropriate screening.

Screenings, not just symbolism

Unlike purely symbolic initiatives, the PCB partnered with the Pink Ribbon Breast Cancer Trust Hospital to provide tangible healthcare resources: free mammogram screenings were offered to female spectators and local residents between October 24 and 26. The board also introduced pink-themed limited edition merchandise, with proceeds going towards the treatment of those who cannot afford it, and held an auction of autographed jerseys from Pakistan stars Shaheen Afridi and Babar Azam, with the proceeds going towards the same cause. This is not the first time Pakistan have worn pink jerseys to support breast cancer awareness — in October 2025, the team wore a special pink kit during a T20I against South Africa in Rawalpindi — but bringing the initiative to an ODI fixture, on the same day as a famous one-wicket win, gave Pink Day its biggest stage yet.
